clue.text: Worn-out horse, say, given minute examination

indicators.note: say tells us to use only how the word for a worn-out horse is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a screw is an old word for a broken-down, worn-out horse
minute (my-NEWT) means very small, tiny

explanation.surface: A tired old nag is being given a very close inspection, perhaps by a vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes the old-horse word SCREW stand only for its sound, written SCRU. 'minute' is read as my-NEWT (tiny), not as a unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close, careful inspection, a synonym for a thorough examination.

clue.text: Scrap university course in fit of temper

indicators.note: in tells us the degree course sits inside the word for a fit of temper

parts.note: a snit is a fit of irritation or pique
PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a well-known Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: Someone throws away their university course in a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a famous Oxford University degree. 'Scrap' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment, just as a scrap is.

clue.text: Criminal always at root of noisy disturbance

indicators.note: at root of places the word for always beneath, so after, the word for the noisy disturbance in this down clue

parts.note: a racket is a loud din or commotion
e'er is a poetic shortening of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A crook is always behind any loud disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'at root of' puts E'ER (poetic for 'ever', always) at the bottom, under RACKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a criminal who runs a dishonest or extortionate business.

clue.text: African state university involved in development of 24

indicators.note: involved in means the letter for university is wrapped up inside the rearranged letters
development of signals the letters of entry 24 are worked into a new form

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, the dye ingredient

explanation.surface: An African country's university is involved in developing a dye ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges ISATIN, the answer to 24 across, and 'involved in' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country in North Africa, so it is an African state.

clue.text: Famously includes 1950s youth in only novel

indicators.note: includes tells us the shuffled word contains the youth from the 1950s
novel means new, so the letters of only are put in a new order

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a fashionable British youth of the 1950s

explanation.surface: Something famously features a 1950s youth in just one novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the letters of 'only' into NOLY, and 'includes' wraps it round the youth. A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth who wore Edwardian-style clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Notedly means in a well-known or notable way, which is what famously means.

clue.text: Page from story of sower identifies farmland

indicators.note: from shows the page letter taken away from the longer word

parts.note: the Parable of the Sower is one of Jesus's stories in the Gospels

explanation.surface: A page taken from the biblical story of the sower mentions fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes P (page) away from PARABLE. The Parable of the Sower is a Gospel story about seed falling on different ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is farmland used for growing crops, and the word is also used as a noun for such land.

clue.text: George greatly welcomes a place that's perfect, almost

indicators.note: welcomes means the word for greatly takes the perfect place inside it

parts.note: a lot means greatly, very much

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the perfect place is dropped

parts.note: Utopia is an imaginary perfect place

explanation.surface: A man called George greatly welcomes somewhere nearly perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final A of the perfect place, and 'welcomes' puts what is left inside. In Britain 'George' is old pilots' slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George is old British pilots' slang for the automatic pilot, the system that flies a plane by itself.

clue.text: As it briefly appears, it's associated with old lace

definitions.meaning: As is the chemical symbol, the short written form, of this element
... and Old Lace is a well-known stage play and film comedy

explanation.definitionFit: As is the symbol for the poisonous element, and the element is paired with old lace in the title of the famous comedy.

clue.text: Thrash dunce, finally, in state of agitation

indicators.note: in tells us the final letter goes inside the word for agitation

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated or flustered

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word dunce

explanation.surface: Someone beats a slow pupil while in a worked-up state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E, the end of 'dunce', and 'in' puts it inside LATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: To leather someone is to beat them hard, as with a leather strap, so it means to thrash.

clue.text: Tin cans not recycled? How irregular

indicators.note: recycled means the letters are processed and remade into a new order

explanation.surface: Tin cans that were not recycled raise the question of how erratic the collection is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges the ten letters of TIN CANS NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconstant keeps changing and is not steady, so it is irregular.

clue.text: TV programme made in a bar?

definitions.meaning: a long-running television drama serial about everyday lives
the washing product that is sold shaped as a bar, not a pub

explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a TV serial, and the washing product comes in a bar.

clue.text: Delighted about land contract, quiet duke has a second drink

indicators.note: about means the quiet and duke letters are placed around the land contract

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
a lease is a contract for renting land or property
s is the abbreviation for a second of time
punch is a mixed drink, often of fruit juice and spirits

explanation.surface: A duke, happy about a quiet land deal, has another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the contract between the two single letters: P is the music marking for quiet, as in piano. 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pleased as punch is an idiom for being delighted.

clue.text: People generally accept blame for such treatment

indicators.note: accept means the word for people takes the word for blame inside it

parts.note: they means people in general, as in 'they say'
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Most people accept blame when they undergo such treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the rap' is the idiom behind blame; 'they' is the vague people of 'they say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment for a physical or mental illness.

clue.text: Farm worker wearily plodding homeward to lunch?

definitions.meaning: echoes Gray's Elegy: the man with the plough homeward plods his weary way
a pub lunch of bread, cheese and pickle

explanation.definitionFit: The man in Gray's poem who plods home is a plough worker, and a ploughman's is a cold British pub lunch.

clue.text: Oddball employed by port authority gives notice

indicators.note: employed by places the oddball after the authority, as if working for it

parts.note: the PLA is the Port of London Authority
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: An eccentric working for the harbour authorities puts up a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Port of London Authority runs the Thames port. 'employed by' puts the eccentric after it, as if on its payroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster, a public notice.

clue.text: A very quiet part of London, and so attractive

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
Ealing is a borough in west London

explanation.surface: A peaceful London district is a lovely place.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the music marking for very quiet. EALING is a district in west London, known for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing means pleasing or attractive.

clue.text: Start to speak, and encourage the operator

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of the word speak

parts.note: to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to begin speaking and to cheer on the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' takes S from 'speak', followed by URGE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is the person who carries out operations, so an operator in the medical sense.

clue.text: Raw spud thrown in direction of ceiling

indicators.note: thrown means the letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncooked potato is tossed up towards the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges the letters of RAW SPUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Upwards means towards a higher point, the direction of the ceiling.

clue.text: Dashing fellow in high-performance car

indicators.note: in means the man's name goes inside the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a fast touring car
Allan is a man's name, so a fellow

explanation.surface: A dashing man drives a fast sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing fellow' reads as one phrase, but only 'Dashing' is the definition; 'fellow' gives a man's name, which 'in' puts inside the fast-car label.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means brave and stylish, close to dashing in sense.

clue.text: Sound procedure for establishing Eurasian grasslands

indicators.note: Sound tells us the answer is spoken like the word for a procedure

parts.note: the steps are the stages in a procedure for setting something up

explanation.surface: A reliable method is needed to set up the plains of Eurasia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like the adjective 'reliable' but it signals a word heard aloud: STEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppes are the vast treeless plains stretching across Eastern Europe and Asia.

clue.text: South American president's initial anger makes us sigh

parts.note: US means American, as in US troops

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of the word president's

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A South American president's first outburst of fury leaves us sighing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes P from 'president's'. 'South American' looks like one phrase but splits into S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspire is a literary verb meaning to breathe out, to sigh.

clue.text: Hold captive in French mountain range

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a chain is a line of linked mountains

explanation.surface: Someone is held prisoner in a French mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchain is to bind in chains, to hold captive.

clue.text: Platoon officer brought in to complete retreat

indicators.note: brought in to means the officer is placed inside the word for complete

parts.note: sheer means complete or utter, as in sheer folly
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, who commands a platoon

explanation.surface: A platoon's lieutenant is brought in to make the retreat a full one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' is the noun, a safe hiding place, not the military withdrawal that 'Platoon' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place of refuge, a retreat.

clue.text: Hopeless pursuit for an ornithologist

definitions.meaning: a search that is pointless and bound to fail
read literally, a bird-watcher might chase after an untamed goose

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a hopeless search, and literally describes chasing a wild bird that a bird expert might track.

clue.text: Part of opera in which Callas loses her head?

indicators.note: loses her head means the singer's first name drops its first letter

parts.note: Maria Callas was a famous opera soprano

explanation.surface: A dramatic moment in an opera where the diva is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Callas was a famous Greek-American soprano; 'loses her head' removes the M of MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song, part of an opera.

clue.text: Note attached to a catalogue of abstract art

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A remark is pinned to the catalogue for an abstract art exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as a written remark but it is the musical note MINIM (a half note).
explanation.definitionFit: Minimalist describes a spare style of abstract art that uses very few elements.

clue.text: Dye ingredient this writer demonstrated

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I
to sit in is to protest by occupying a place, so sat in means demonstrated

explanation.surface: The writer explains a dye component they personally demonstrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstrated' means protested: to stage a sit-in is to sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is an orange-red compound used in making dyes such as indigo.

clue.text: One may or may not be in the majority

definitions.text: One may or may not be in the majority

parts.words: One may or may not be in the majority
parts.note: majority read as the age of legal adulthood: a person aged eighteen or nineteen has reached it, a younger one has not

explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged thirteen to nineteen may be past the age of majority, eighteen, or still below it.
